# Statements, directives, keywords and types

## Declarations

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `DIM name[(bounds)] [AS type] [= value] [, …]` | Declares variables or arrays, with a type and optionally a first value; inside a SUB or FUNCTION, locals. `DIM m` with no type is a DOUBLE. |
| `REDIM [PRESERVE] name(bounds) [AS type]` | Resizes an array that exists (or creates it); the elements whose indexes are still inside the new bounds keep their values. |
| `STATIC name[(bounds)] AS type` | Inside a SUB or FUNCTION, declares a local variable that keeps its value from one call to the next. |
| `CONST name [AS type] = expression` | Names a value fixed for the whole program: `CONST MaxItems = 3`, `CONST Limit AS LONG = 100`. One constant to a CONST: a list (`CONST a = 1, b = 2`) is an error, so write a CONST for each. |
| `DEFINT name [= value] [, …]` | Declares INTEGER (32-bit) variables or arrays, optionally with first values (`DEFINT k(1 TO 3) = {7, 8, 9}`). |
| `DEFSTR name [= value] [, …]` | Declares STRING variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFBYTE name [= value] [, …]` | Declares BYTE variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFWORD name [= value] [, …]` | Declares WORD variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFDWORD name [= value] [, …]` | Declares DWORD variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFLNG name [= value] [, …] (also DEFLONG)` | Declares LONG variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFLONG name [= value] [, …]` | The same as DEFLNG, under the longer name. |
| `DEFSHORT name [= value] [, …]` | Declares SHORT variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFSNG name [= value] [, …]` | Declares SINGLE variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFDBL name [= value] [, …]` | Declares DOUBLE variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `DEFCUR name [= value] [, …]` | Declares CURRENCY variables or arrays, optionally with first values. |
| `GLOBAL name AS type (also PUBLIC / PRIVATE before a declaration)` | VB's scope words, accepted so such programs compile: `GLOBAL` / `PUBLIC` / `PRIVATE` before a declaration, SUB or FUNCTION declare it as without them. |

## Types and objects

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `TYPE name [EXTENDS type] … END TYPE (also STRUCT … END STRUCT)` | Defines a record type: fields, and optionally methods, a CONSTRUCTOR, events and a parent type to inherit from (`EXTENDS`). `STRUCT` is another name for it. |
| `TYPE name EXTENDS QOBJECT\|component` | Makes a TYPE inherit another TYPE's members, or makes it a component of your own built on a component (`EXTENDS RButton`). |
| `PROPERTY SET name(value AS type) … END PROPERTY` | In a TYPE: the routine that runs when a program assigns to the property `name`, given the value assigned. |
| `EVENT(member) … END EVENT` | In a TYPE that extends a component: the code run when the component's event happens (`EVENT OnClick … END EVENT`). |
| `CONSTRUCTOR … END CONSTRUCTOR` | In a TYPE: code that runs when a variable of the type is created, to set its fields' first values. |
| `PUBLIC: / PRIVATE: in a TYPE` | In a TYPE: `PUBLIC:` and `PRIVATE:` start sections of members; accepted, and access isn't enforced. |
| `CREATE name AS type … END CREATE` | Creates a component (or object) and sets its properties and events in the block; components created inside it get it as their parent. |
| `WITH object … END WITH` | Inside the block, `.Member` refers to a member of the object named: `WITH Form … .Caption = "Hi" … END WITH`. |

## Routines

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `SUB name[(params)] … END SUB` | Defines a routine that returns no value; it is called by its name, arguments without parentheses (`Greet "you"`). |
| `FUNCTION name[(params)] AS type … END FUNCTION` | Defines a routine that returns a value: assign it to the function's name (or `Result`) inside the body. |
| `SUBI name(…) … END SUBI` | Defines a SUB that takes any number of arguments, read inside with `PARAMVAL`, `PARAMSTR$`, `PARAMVALCOUNT` and `PARAMSTRCOUNT`. |
| `FUNCTIONI name(…) AS type … END FUNCTIONI` | Defines a FUNCTION that takes any number of arguments, read inside with `PARAMVAL`, `PARAMSTR$`, `PARAMVALCOUNT` and `PARAMSTRCOUNT`. |
| `DECLARE SUB\|FUNCTION name [LIB "file" [ALIAS "name"]] [(params)] [AS type]` | Declares a SUB or FUNCTION ahead of its body, or one in a DLL (`LIB`), which runs for real on Windows, interpreted and in native builds: numbers go by value unless `BYREF`, STRINGs and TYPEs by address. What the DLL writes into them (also later, as a driver fills a buffer it was given) reaches the program at its next event, wait (`DOEVENTS`, `SLEEP`) or DLL call. On macOS, Linux and the web the call is an error that names the function. |
| `CALL name[(args)]` | Calls a SUB (the arguments then in parentheses); calling it by its name alone does the same. |
| `BIND pointer TO routine` | Stores the address of a SUB or FUNCTION in a variable, for `CALLFUNC`. |

## Flow

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `EXIT FOR \| DO \| WHILE \| SUB \| FUNCTION` | Leaves the innermost FOR, DO or WHILE loop, or the SUB or FUNCTION, at once. |
| `IF condition THEN … [ELSEIF condition THEN …] [ELSE …] END IF` | Runs statements when a condition is true (non-zero), others with ELSEIF or ELSE; on one line, `IF c THEN … ELSE …` needs no END IF. |
| `SELECT CASE expression … CASE values … CASE ELSE … END SELECT` | Runs the first CASE whose values match the expression: single values, `a TO b` ranges, `IS > n` comparisons, lists of them; CASE ELSE when none does. |
| `FOR variable [AS type] = start TO end [STEP step] … NEXT [variable]` | Runs the body for each value of a counter from `start` to `end`, adding `step` (1 when not given) each time. `FOR i AS INTEGER = 1 TO n` also declares the counter where it isn't declared yet — a local in a SUB or FUNCTION; a counter already declared with the same type is that variable, one of another type is an error. |
| `WHILE condition … WEND` | Runs the body as long as the condition is true, testing it before each pass. |
| `DO [WHILE\|UNTIL condition] … LOOP [WHILE\|UNTIL condition]` | A loop: tested at the top (`DO WHILE` / `DO UNTIL`), at the bottom (`LOOP WHILE` / `LOOP UNTIL`), or not at all (left with `EXIT DO`). |
| `GOTO label` | Continues the program at a label or line number. |
| `GOSUB label … RETURN` | Jumps to a label; the `RETURN` there comes back to the statement after the GOSUB. |
| `RETURN` | Goes back to the statement after the last `GOSUB`. |
| `END [exit code]` | Ends the program at once; files it wrote are kept. `END n` ends it with exit code n, a number or numeric expression stored as a LONG is, so a console tool can fail a build: `IF failures > 0 THEN END 1`. A bare name must be one the program declared (`END code` after `DIM code AS INTEGER = 5`); `END SUBB`, a typo of a block's ending, and an undeclared name are syntax errors. 0 means success, and a plain `END` ends with 0. The shell reads it with `echo $?` (macOS, Linux) or `echo %ERRORLEVEL%` (Windows); macOS and Linux keep the low 8 bits. In a web page there is no exit code: the program ends and the number is ignored. `END IF`, `END SUB` and the like close blocks. |
| `ON ERROR RESUME NEXT \| GOTO label` | VB's error trapping, accepted so such programs compile and ignored: a run-time error still ends the program. |

## Console

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `PRINT [expression][; \| ,] …` | Writes values to the console and ends the line, unless the last is followed by `;` or `,` (no print zones). `?` is short for PRINT. |
| `LPRINT [expression][; \| ,] …` | Prints to the printer as `PRINT` prints to the console; `LFLUSH` sends the job. |
| `INPUT ["prompt";] variable` | Shows the prompt, reads a line typed at the console and stores it in the variable (as a number for a numeric one). |

## Files

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `LINE INPUT #n, variable` | Reads a whole line, commas included, from a file opened for INPUT into a string variable. |
| `OPEN file FOR INPUT\|OUTPUT\|APPEND\|BINARY\|RANDOM AS #n` | Opens a file under a number: `INPUT` to read lines, `OUTPUT` to write a new file, `APPEND` to add to one, `BINARY` or `RANDOM` for bytes. |
| `CLOSE #n` | Closes the file opened under that number; what was written to it is kept. |
| `PRINT #n, expression [; …]` | Writes values to a file opened for OUTPUT or APPEND, as PRINT writes them to the console. |
| `WRITE #n, expression [, …]` | Writes values to a file separated by commas, strings in quotes, so `INPUT #` can read them back. |
| `INPUT #n, variable [, …]` | Reads comma-separated values from a file opened for INPUT into variables. |
| `SEEK #n, position` | Moves to a byte of an open file (1 the first): the next read or write is there. |

## Data

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `DATA value [, …]` | Lists values in the program for `READ` to read, in order. |
| `READ variable [, …]` | Stores the next values from the program's `DATA` lists in variables. |
| `RESTORE [label]` | Makes the next `READ` start again from the first `DATA` value, or from the first after a label. |
| `SWAP a, b` | Exchanges the values of two variables or array elements. |
| `INC variable [, amount]` | Adds `amount` (1 when not given) to a variable. |
| `DEC variable [, amount]` | Subtracts `amount` (1 when not given) from a variable. |
| `QUICKSORT(array(first), array(last), ASCEND\|DESCEND)` | Sorts an array's elements from `first` to `last` in place, numbers by value and strings by their characters; ASCEND (0) sorts upward, DESCEND (1) downward. |

## Other

| Statement | |
|---|---|
| `REM comment (also ' comment)` | A comment: the rest of the line is ignored. `'` does the same, also after a statement. |
| `IMPORT "module" [AS alias]` | Names a module; accepted and without effect (RapidR's builtins and components need no import). |
| `RUSTSTART … RUSTEND (Rust code, native builds)` | Puts Rust code in the program, up to `RUSTEND`; only in native builds (the interpreter and the web refuse it). |

## Directives

| Directive | |
|---|---|
| `$INCLUDE "file"` | Includes another source file at this point. The include folders and `\` paths work; `RAPIDQ.INC` is built in. |
| `$RESOURCE name AS "file"` | Builds a file into the program as a resource, for `RESOURCE(n)`, `EXTRACTRESOURCE`, `PLAYWAV` and pictures. |
| `$DEFINE name [text]` | Defines a name for `$IFDEF` and, with text, replaces the name by the text in the lines that follow. |
| `$UNDEF name` | Removes a name defined with `$DEFINE`. |
| `$IFDEF name` | Compiles the lines up to `$ELSE` or `$ENDIF` only when the name is defined. |
| `$IFNDEF name` | Compiles the lines up to `$ELSE` or `$ENDIF` only when the name is not defined. |
| `$ELSE` | Starts the lines compiled when the `$IFDEF` / `$IFNDEF` test fails. |
| `$ENDIF` | Ends a `$IFDEF` / `$IFNDEF` block. |
| `$MACRO name(params) = text` | Defines a macro with parameters: each use is replaced by the text, its parameters by the arguments. |
| `$APPTYPE GUI \| CONSOLE \| CGI` | The program's kind: `CONSOLE`, `GUI` or `CGI` (and RapidR's `WEB`). Without it, a program that creates components is a GUI program. |
| `$TYPECHECK ON \| OFF` | `ON`: from here, storing into a variable never declared (DIM, CONST, a parameter) is a compile error; `OFF` turns the check off. |
| `$OPTIMIZE ON \| OFF` | The optimizer switch; accepted, with nothing for RapidR to change. |
| `$ESCAPECHARS ON \| OFF` | `ON`: strings in this file understand escapes (`\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\`, `\x41`); `OFF` (the default) reads them as written. |
| `$OPTION ICON "file" \| DECIMAL \| BYREF \| INKEY$ TRAPALL \| EXPLICIT \| WEAKTYPE ON \| OFF …` | Program options: `ICON "file"` the program's icon (the executable's, and its windows'; a file that isn't there is a compile error; the last `ICON` wins; an .ico, .icns, .png or .svg file), `DECIMAL` VAL's decimal character, `BYREF` parameters by reference, `EXPLICIT` as `$TYPECHECK ON`, `INKEY$ TRAPALL`, `DIM type`, and, in a classic program (`.bas`, `.rqw`, `.rqb`), `WEAKTYPE ON` / `OFF`: with `ON` a CONST can be written again (also `Public Const`) with no error and the last value wins, even of another type, as the classic compiler has it — the VB constants files older programs include start with it ON and end with it OFF; with `OFF` (the default) a second CONST of a name is `CONST variable A already defined`. A `.rr` program has no such option. |
| `$THEME name` | The look the program's windows are drawn in. `RapidR` (the default, also with no `$THEME`): RapidR's own look, as RapidR Studio has it — light, dark or high contrast as the system is set, Inter for the default font; `RapidR Light`, `RapidR Dark`, `RapidR High Contrast` choose one. `Classic`: the classic Windows look, exactly. The older names stay: `Modern`, `Dark` and `HighContrast` are RapidR's light, dark and high-contrast looks; `System`, `Light`, `Windows`, `Win95`, `Win98` and `Win2K` the classic one. A theme changes how things are drawn, never a size or a place; the colours a program sets are drawn as it set them, the system colours (`clBtnFace` …) are the theme's. |

## Keywords and operators

| Keyword | |
|---|---|
| `AND` | Bitwise AND of two 32-bit integers (`7 AND 3` is 3); with comparisons, both must be true. |
| `OR` | Bitwise OR of two 32-bit integers; with comparisons, either may be true. |
| `XOR` | Bitwise exclusive OR of two 32-bit integers; with comparisons, exactly one is true. |
| `NOT` | Bitwise NOT of a 32-bit integer (`NOT 0` is -1); it binds more loosely than comparisons. |
| `MOD` | The remainder of an integer division; its operands are rounded half to even first (`7 MOD 3` is 1). |
| `SHL` | `a SHL n`: a's 32 bits shifted left by n. |
| `SHR` | `a SHR n`: a's 32 bits shifted right by n, zeros coming in. |
| `INV` | `a INV m`: the inverse of a modulo m (`3 INV 26` is 9), -1 when there is none. |
| `IS` | In `CASE IS > n` (and the other comparisons): compares the SELECT CASE expression. |
| `AS` | Gives a type: `DIM x AS INTEGER`, a parameter's, a FUNCTION's result; also `CREATE name AS type`, `OPEN … AS #n`, `$RESOURCE name AS "file"`. |
| `TO` | A range: `FOR i = 1 TO 10`, array bounds `DIM a(1 TO 5)`, `CASE 1 TO 9`; also `BIND p TO routine`. |
| `STEP` | In FOR: the amount added to the counter each pass (negative to count down). |
| `THEN` | Ends an IF or ELSEIF condition; what follows on the same line is a one-line IF. |
| `ELSE` | In IF: the statements run when no condition was true; `CASE ELSE` in SELECT CASE. |
| `ELSEIF` | In IF: another condition, tested when those before it were false. |
| `NEXT` | Ends a FOR loop; the counter's name after it is optional. |
| `WEND` | Ends a WHILE loop. |
| `LOOP` | Ends a DO loop, optionally with its `WHILE` or `UNTIL` test. |
| `UNTIL` | In DO … LOOP: loop until the condition becomes true. |
| `CASE` | In SELECT CASE: the values the next statements run for; `CASE ELSE` for any other. |
| `LIB` | In DECLARE: the shared library a routine is in. |
| `ALIAS` | In DECLARE … LIB: the routine's name in the library, when the program calls it by another. |
| `BYVAL` | A parameter passed by value: the routine gets a copy (the default, unless `$OPTION BYREF`). |
| `BYREF` | A parameter passed by reference: the routine's changes reach the caller's variable. |
| `PRESERVE` | In REDIM, VB's word for keeping an array's values; RapidR's REDIM keeps them anyway. |
| `SET` | In `PROPERTY SET`: the routine that runs when the property is assigned. |
| `STRUCT` | Another name for TYPE: `STRUCT … END STRUCT` defines a record type. |
| `PRIVATE` | In a TYPE, `PRIVATE:` starts a section of members (access isn't enforced); before a declaration, VB's scope word, accepted. |
| `PROTECTED` | In a TYPE, `PROTECTED:` starts a section of members, as PRIVATE: and PUBLIC: do (access isn't enforced). |
| `THIS` | Inside a TYPE's methods: the instance the method was called on (`This.Count`). |
| `SUPER` | Inside a TYPE that extends another: the parent type's members, as in `Super.Method`. |
| `RUSTEND` | Ends a `RUSTSTART` block of Rust code. |

## Types

| Type | |
|---|---|
| `BYTE` | 8-bit unsigned integer, 0 to 255; a store wraps (`300` holds 44). Suffix `?`. |
| `SHORT` | 16-bit signed integer, -32,768 to 32,767; a store wraps. Suffix `%`. |
| `WORD` | 16-bit unsigned integer, 0 to 65,535; a store wraps. Suffix `??`. |
| `INTEGER` | 32-bit signed integer, -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647, the same as LONG; a store truncates a fraction. |
| `DWORD` | 32-bit integer, signed (-2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647). Suffix `???`. |
| `LONG` | 32-bit signed integer, -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647; a store truncates a fraction. Suffix `&`. |
| `SINGLE` | 32-bit floating-point number, about 7 significant digits. Suffix `!`. |
| `DOUBLE` | 64-bit floating-point number, about 15 significant digits. Suffix `#`. |
| `STRING` | Text of any length, counted in characters; `STRING * n` always holds n characters. Suffix `$`. |
| `VARIANT` | Holds whatever is stored in it: a number, text or object. An undeclared variable is one. |
| `QOBJECT` | The base type of objects: `TYPE name EXTENDS RObject` makes a TYPE with methods, a constructor and inheritance. |
| `INT64` | A 64-bit signed whole number, from -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807. Its value keeps its type wherever it goes (a VARIANT, an array, a TYPE field, a property, the debugger, JSON): PRINT, STR$, `&` and `+` with text show every digit; `+ - *` wrap at 64 bits; `\`, MOD and the comparisons are exact, against a DOUBLE too; AND, OR, XOR, NOT, SHL, SHR work on all 64 bits; a FOR counter stops at its type's end. A DOUBLE stored into it is truncated toward zero (out of range: -9223372036854775808); text is read as VAL reads it, to the last digit. Beside an INT64, a literal is read as written: `&H` up to 16 digits (`&HFFFFFFFF` is 4294967295), decimals up to 18446744073709551615. With a DOUBLE in the expression the result is a DOUBLE, as usual. |
| `UINT64` | A 64-bit unsigned whole number, from 0 to 18446744073709551615. It works as INT64 does, unsigned: shown, compared and divided as the unsigned number it is wherever it goes. With an INT64 in the same expression the result is a UINT64; a comparison is exact (a UINT64 above 9223372036854775807 is greater than any INT64, and `u > -1` is true). A DOUBLE stored into it that is negative or too big gives 0; a whole number keeps its 64 bits (-1 is 18446744073709551615). `FOR u = 10 TO 0 STEP -1` stops at 0. |
| `UINT32` | A 32-bit unsigned whole number, from 0 to 4294967295 (DWORD is the 32-bit signed type). A store keeps the low 32 bits (`-1` is 4294967295, `&HF58ACBFB` 4119514107); its value is worked out in 64 bits, so `u * 2` doesn't overflow, and PRINT shows every digit. HEX$ shows 8 digits. A DOUBLE stored into it that is negative or too big gives 0. |
| `CURRENCY` | A number for amounts of money; RapidR keeps it as a 64-bit floating-point number. |
| `ROBJECT` | RapidR's name for QOBJECT, the base type of objects: `TYPE name EXTENDS ROBJECT`. |
